review.reason: Scaling each operand before summation loses significant cancellation information. On C11 platforms with 64-bit long-double precision, inputs 100000000000000000000 and -99999999999999999992 have mean 4.000000, but normalization rounds their difference and yields approximately 2.710505. Compensated summation cannot recover precision lost during division. The evaluator misses this case. Changes are implementation-only with no apparent evaluator gaming; this finding is analytical, not an executed test.

The running mean loses small contributions during cancellation. For example, arguments 1e100, 1, -1e100 have mean 0.333333, but the contribution of 1 is rounded away, producing zero or a large rounding residual. The evaluator does not cover this case. The change stays within implementation scope and shows no evaluator gaming, but needs more robust accumulation.
